BREAKING: Malaysia's exports surged +54.5% YoY in September, to a record $52.7 billion, their largest YoY increase since April 2021.

Malaysia’s exports have now seen above +35.0% YoY growth for 6 consecutive months, the longest such streak since the 1970s.

The surge has been driven by manufactured goods, which rose +58.6% YoY and accounted for 89.1% of total exports.

Electrical and electronic product exports rose +69.2% YoY amid strong global demand for AI-related products.

Exports surged +175.2% to Taiwan, +89.9% to the US, +50.4% to Singapore, +35.3% to the EU, and +22.1% to China.

The global AI investment boom is driving an unprecedented surge in Asian trade.

Gold stocks have rarely been this oversold.

~92% of stocks in the gold miners ETF, $GDX, are now trading below their 50-day moving average, the highest proportion since late July.

This figure has risen +80 percentage points in just 21 sessions.

Furthermore, 90% of stocks in $GDX are trading below their 200-day moving average, the highest proportion in 3 months.

Similar setups occurred in March 2024 and December 2024.

In the following month, $GDX rallied +21.5% and +15.4%, respectively.

History suggests the selloff in gold miners is nearing exhaustion.

BREAKING: The Memory ETF, $DRAM, has posted -$2.0 billion in outflows so far in October, putting the fund on track for its largest monthly withdrawal since launching on April 2nd.

This would also mark its 3rd consecutive monthly outflow, following -$1.6 billion in September and -$400 million in August.

Last week alone, $DRAM saw -$105 million in outflows, its 9th consecutive weekly withdrawal.

As a result, the fund is down -23% month-to-date, trading near its lowest level since early May.

Yet, $DRAM is still up +70% since inception, after recording a +190% gain in mid-June.

Meanwhile, the 2x leveraged long Memory ETF, $RAM, is down -66% since its June 24th debut.

The memory chip trade has seen a major pullback.

BREAKING: The S&P Global US Manufacturing PMI index rose +0.1 point in October, to 56.0, its highest level since May 2022.

This exceeded expectations of a -0.4 point decline.

The improvement was particularly driven by job growth, which rose to its strongest level since March 2012.

Meanwhile, the Services PMI index fell -0.9 points, to 57.9, its 2nd-highest level in 4 years.

This brought the Composite PMI index down -0.8 points, to 57.6, also its 2nd-highest in 4 years.

Despite the slight decline, these readings point to GDP growth of +5.0% at an annualized rate in Q4 2026, following projected growth of +4.0% in Q3 2026.

US economic growth is booming amid the AI Revolution.

US equity market breadth is rapidly improving:

The proportion of S&P 500 stocks trading above their 50-day moving average surged +5 percentage points on Friday, to 61%, the highest reading since mid-August.

Since the October 1st intraday low, this figure has more than tripled.

Additionally, the proportion of S&P 500 stocks trading above their 200-day moving average rose +3 percentage points on Friday, to 57%, the most since September 9th.

Over the last 3 weeks, this figure has risen +17 percentage points.

This comes despite the S&P 500 remaining roughly unchanged over the same period.

This also ranks among the 3 sharpest improvements in market breadth over the last 3 years.

On Thursday alone, 335 S&P 500 stocks finished higher, despite the index declining -1.2% on that day.

The market is strengthening beneath the surface.

AI is generating massive fortunes in the US and China:

The combined wealth of new US AI billionaire entrants rose +$44 billion in the first 9 months of 2026, to $132 billion.

Over the same time period, the combined wealth of new Chinese AI billionaire entrants surged +$43 billion, to $89 billion.

This metric tracks the combined net worth of people who newly entered the world’s 500 richest list in 2026 through AI-related businesses.

This includes 12 billionaires from the US and 5 from China.

As a result, the combined wealth of this group in the US and China soared +$87 billion, to $221 billion.

AI is creating unprecedented amounts of wealth.
